summary.title: No triggers hit. A few things worth knowing
summary.text: Nothing here calls for action. The amber items are background to be aware of.

items.question: Is the recession warning on?
items.text: The 10-year rate is 0.88 points above the 3-month rate. No sale can trigger until that gap drops below zero.
items.trigger: The curve inverts again and the warning switches back on

items.question: Are interest rates too low for the yield curve to work?
items.text: Short-term rates are well above zero, so the yield curve can still invert and warn.
items.trigger: The Fed cuts rates to about 0.5% or less

items.group: Backups, if the yield curve stops working
items.question: Backup 1: is unemployment rising?
items.text: Unemployment is at or below its 12-month average. It only matters if rates fall near zero; until then the yield curve is the warning.

items.group: Backups, if the yield curve stops working
items.question: Backup 2: are company bonds under stress?
items.text: Lenders aren't asking much more to hold riskier company bonds than six months ago. This is the second backup, for a long stretch of near-zero rates. It gave false alarms in 2010-2016, so it is watched, not acted on.
kv: Gap between riskier and safest company bonds

items.question: How much of the S&P 500 is its ten biggest companies?
items.text: The three largest are Apple Inc, Nvidia Corp and Microsoft Corp. That is far above the historical norm, and the Nasdaq-100 fund holds many of the same companies at higher weights. Selling the whole Nasdaq slice on a signal is the protection.
kv: Ten largest companies' share of the S&P 500
items.trigger: Top-10 concentration passes 50% of the S&P 500

items.question: Is the Nasdaq-100 slice still pulling its weight?
items.text: The Nasdaq-100 is ahead of the S&P 500 over the last five years.
items.source: FRED: NASDAQ100 and SP500 (prices, before dividends)
items.trigger: The Nasdaq trails the S&P by more than 2% a year over 5 years
items.now: Nasdaq +1.9% a year vs. the S&P 500

items.question: Would the safe side hold up if a sale happened now?
items.text: Treasuries lost a little over the last year as rates rose, while T-bills kept earning. The half-and-half split limits the damage.
items.source: FRED: GS10 and TB3MS (Treasury return rebuilt from yields)

items.question: Have recent sales been costing money?
items.text: No false alarms in the last two years.
kv: Sales in the last two years
items.source: This site's backtest of the 70/30 option
items.trigger: One sale costs more than 10% of the account, or three false alarms happen within two years

items.question: Do the historical tests still give the same answers?
items.text: Every update reruns the backtest on the fixed history and compares it with the expected result. They match.
kv: Latest S&P 500 price in the data
items.source: Rerun on every update from pipeline/rules.py
items.trigger: The historical tests stop matching their expected results

items.question: What are stocks priced to return over the next decade?
items.text: Published 10-year outlooks are well below the roughly 10% a year stocks returned historically. Plan around the low and middle projections, not the backtest.
